eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects high uncertainty in forecast models for São Paulo's highest temperature on May 11, with implied probabilities tightly clustered at 37.5% for 20°C, 37.0% for 18°C, and 36.0% for 21°C, driven by an advancing cold front from the South. INMET's May 4-11 weekly outlook indicates mostly stable weather in the Southeast with low cloudiness and possible weak showers in southern São Paulo, but the front's timing could introduce southerly winds, increased cloud cover, and rain that suppress peak daytime heating below May climatological averages of 22-23°C. Model ensembles diverge on frontal passage speed—earlier arrival favors 18-19°C maxima via cooler air advection, while delays allow 20-21°C—pending tomorrow's updated INMET and CPTEC guidance. Urban heat island effects at official stations like Mirante de Santana add minor variability to observations.

Historical May 11 averages 20°C, but urban heat moderation and peak heating timing create genuine uncertainty; watch KMA's 11 AM KST update for refinements before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) and ECMWF ensemble forecasts indicate a high near 16-17°C in Munich on May 11, driven by an approaching low-pressure system bringing increased cloud cover and shower risks after recent warm highs around 22°C on May 9. Model consensus shows the GFS slightly warmer at 18°C in drier scenarios, while ECMWF leans cooler with persistent overcast conditions limiting solar heating and surface temperatures. Trader sentiment reflects this spread, with 34.5% implied probability for 16°C versus 29.5% for 17°C, highlighting uncertainty in frontal boundary timing and precipitation amounts. New model runs overnight and DWD updates by morning could refine odds ahead of resolution based on official airport observations. Historical mid-May averages hover around 18°C, underscoring the transient cool-down.
